A solid rectangular block resting on its largest flat face next to the same block standing upright on its smallest face. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A simple mercury barometer. A long glass tube is inverted in a reservoir (dish) of mercury. Arrows point down on the mercury surface in the dish, labelled 'Atmospheric pressure'. A vertical bracket measures the height of the mercury in the tube from the dish's liquid surface to the top of the column, labelled 'h = 760 mm'. The empty space at the very top of the closed tube is labelled 'Torricellian vacuum'.

A cross-section diagram of an aneroid barometer. Shows a corrugated metallic capsule (partially evacuated box) connected to a strong leaf spring. A mechanical lever and gear system connects the spring to a pointer moving over a circular dial marked with pressure values.

A U-tube manometer. The left arm is connected to a round gas flask labelled 'Gas pressure (P_gas)'. The right arm is open to the air, with an arrow labelled 'Atmospheric pressure (P_atm)' pointing in. The liquid (e.g., mercury) is pushed down in the left arm and up in the right arm. A horizontal dotted line shows the lower liquid level in the left arm continuing across to the right arm. A vertical bracket measures the height difference 'h' between the liquid level in the right arm and the dotted line.

Diagram of a hydraulic press. Two vertical cylinders are connected by a horizontal pipe, all filled with a blue liquid. The left cylinder is narrow with a small piston. The right cylinder is wide with a large piston. Dotted lines in the fluid show pressure is equal throughout.
